reasons: The PromQL multiplies the result by a constant 100 that does not appear in the Datadog source; numeric constants not in the source are forbidden, and the scale is not justified by a unit difference (the metric is a plain connection count in {connections}).

The Datadog template variable $host (prefix host, default *) should become a matcher on the host label (e.g. host_name=~"$host"), but the candidate drops it, so the candidate covers all series instead of the same filtered set.
The metric mapping nginx.connections.accepted to nginx.connections_accepted (monotonic sum, in dataset) is plausible, and translating rather than blocking is the correct outcome.
